title: The Starry Night
location: Museum of Modern Art, New York
short_description: A swirling night sky over a quiet village, painted in thick expressive brushstrokes.
long_description: The Starry Night depicts the view from the east-facing window of Vincent van Gogh's room at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Remy-de-Provence, where he was recovering from a mental breakdown. The painting shows a turbulent night sky filled with swirling clouds and bright stars over a peaceful village.
historical_context: Van Gogh painted The Starry Night during a difficult period of his life, while voluntarily committed to a psychiatric hospital. The work represents his personal vision of the night sky rather than a literal record of it.
anecdote: Van Gogh painted the scene during the day from memory, using only his imagination and his recollections of the view from his asylum window.
